title: C315 inline connector reference
introduction:
This inline connector reference groups seat-heater, temperature-sensor, switch, indicator, fan and blower-control connections. It is a little climate-control switchboard: sharing a housing does not give every wire the same job.

I begin with the harness heading and its face drawing, find the cavity label, then read the complete corresponding row. Circuit Number and Function identify the connection’s job; Color, Gauge, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number describe that particular entry. Keep repeated entries separate, including those with different gauge values. Blank qualifiers do not select an applicable configuration.

The numbered banks exchange sides between the drawings. Use the printed labels and housing outlines as page landmarks; the physical terminal-side or wire-side viewing direction is unspecified. Grey positions can be compared with the accompanying rows, but shading alone is not a circuit assignment. Gauge conventions and Size and Used codes remain undefined here. This is a reading reference, with no physical access, connector-release, probing, test-limit or replacement procedure. Differences between the face tables also prevent treating them as a verified through-connection map.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in both drawings and the pigtail cavity count. That discrepancy remains unresolved and does not establish extra physical cavities.

edits.why: The lower-numbered bank is on the left in this drawing. I use the cavity labels to navigate the rounded housing outline. Its visible projections help distinguish the drawing, but their release or locking functions are not identified.

Read the exact Function before grouping a row with nearby seat connections: passenger-indicator entries appear among driver-seat functions. Heater, sensor and blower-control labels describe different electrical jobs. Repeated heater entries with different gauge values remain separate records; no qualifier selects between them. The grey positions correspond here to rows with blank circuit details and no terminal assignment.

The lower-numbered bank is on the right in this drawing. I relocate the printed label when switching faces instead of carrying over its horizontal position. The outline helps with that comparison without establishing the physical viewing direction or a disconnection method.

Keep this table’s circuit, gauge and terminal information together. Some matching cavity labels carry different circuit functions in the male table, including passenger-indicator or driver-switch functions versus driver back-temperature or back-blower-control functions. These differences need reconciliation before tracing a connection through the pair. Do not fill a blank assignment or choose a replacement terminal from the other face’s row.

Keep each kit’s service part, engineering shell, material, gauge and cavity fields together as a separate catalog entry. The two entries for the male shell have different kit and service-part numbers; sharing a shell number does not establish interchangeability or select a repair kit. These listings do not provide installation instructions.

The Product Id is a separate regional catalog listing. The table does not associate it with a particular kit row above or supply installation instructions; do not infer either association from its placement.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count exceeds the numbered cavity positions shown in both face illustrations. The supplied values remain unchanged; the meaning of that count needs reconciliation.

Several corresponding cavity labels have incompatible male and female circuit assignments: passenger-indicator and driver-switch entries differ from driver back-temperature and back-blower-control entries. Blank qualifiers do not explain whether these represent separate configurations or an incorrect association. The faces cannot be presented as a verified through-connection map.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 76 primary units, four complete pages/two figures and six edits. Original first CLI author covered 61 units/four headings. Complete draft adds pigtail and European catalog headings, all table rows and raw text coverage. Original partial author retained separately; physical count, cross-face circuit assignments and gauge applicability remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
